title: How Wind Shapes Deserts
objective: After this level you can explain how wind builds dunes, strips away sand and sandblasts rock.
summary: Only about 20% of deserts are sand. Wind strips fine particles, leaving desert pavement, carves ventifacts and yardangs, and walks dunes downwind by saltation and slipface avalanches.

cards.headline: Only about 20% of Earth's deserts are covered in sand.
cards.body: Picture a desert and you probably see dunes. Most deserts are rock and gravel instead. The wind explains both.

cards.headline: The wind as a vacuum cleaner
cards.body: Wind is good at picking up loose, fine particles, and geologists call that deflation. Blow the fine stuff away long enough and what's left is desert pavement: a sheet of rock fragments fitted together like a cobbled street. Nearly half of desert surfaces are plains of loose gravel stripped this way.

cards.headline: The wind as a sandblaster
cards.body: Wind-driven sand is also an abrasive. Rocks sitting in its path get cut into flat, sometimes polished faces; geologists call them ventifacts. On a bigger scale, desert winds streamline whole ridges called yardangs, up to tens of meters high and kilometers long.

cards.headline: How a dune walks
cards.body: Sand moves mostly by saltation: grains bounce along close to the ground. On a dune, they bounce up the gentle upwind slope. At the crest they pile up until they spill down the steep downwind side, the slipface, in tiny avalanches. Grain by grain, the whole dune moves downwind.

cards.headline: Deserts: read
learned: Only about a fifth of desert is sand
Windblown sand carves ventifacts and yardangs
Dunes move downwind, grain by grain

questions.prompt: Match each desert wind term with its meaning.
questions.explanation: Deflation is wind picking up loose, fine particles, ventifacts are rocks cut into flat, sometimes polished faces, saltation is grains bouncing along, and the slipface is a dune's steep downwind side.

questions.prompt: How does a sand dune move downwind?

options.label: The whole dune slides along on a film of water
options.rationale: Desert dunes are moved by wind, grain by grain.

options.label: Wind blows the sandy crest off and rebuilds the whole dune upwind
options.rationale: The dune moves downwind, not upwind.

options.label: Sand climbs the gentle side, then avalanches down the slipface
The upwind side sinks as the ground settles

questions.explanation: Grains bounce up the gentle upwind slope and spill down the steep slipface, so the dune creeps downwind.

questions.prompt: Desert sand bounces along the ground by saltation. Which part of a river's load can travel the same way?

options.label: Dissolved load
options.rationale: Dissolved minerals travel invisibly, in solution.

options.label: Suspended load
options.rationale: Suspended load is held up in the water.

options.label: Floating ice
options.rationale: A river's load is sediment, not ice.

questions.explanation: A river's bed load is pushed or bounced along the bottom, just as windblown sand saltates across a dune.
